headline: PJM Interconnection, the largest US power grid operator, has warned that data centres are leaving the grid with little room for error.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a direct warning from the operator of a 13-state grid, but one outlet reports it and no reserve figures are given; Souder spoke on 15 Oct 2026, one day before the window.
importance_line: Electricity customers across PJM's 13 states and Washington could face more strain and outage risk during maintenance seasons that used to be calm, though this is the operator's own warning and the article gives no reserve figures.
summary: Newsweek reports that David Souder, executive director of system operations at PJM Interconnection, which coordinates electricity across all or parts of 13 states and the District of Columbia, said on 15 Oct 2026 that year-round data centre demand and unusually warm or cold weather are eroding the quiet spring and autumn periods used to take power plants and lines offline for maintenance, leaving 'little room for error'. Newsweek adds that the Department of Energy issued an emergency order this week to reduce blackout risk in the mid-Atlantic, and that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission rejected a PJM plan to let large new users connect without matching new generation if they accepted possible power cuts.
notes: Read in full. Souder's remarks were on Thursday 15 Oct 2026; Newsweek published 16 Oct 2026. The DOE emergency order of 12 Oct 2026 was in our 14 Oct 2026 edition.
